concepts.title: Prabhat's Change of Heart
concepts.section: Change of Heart, Let us read
concepts.definition: Prabhat starts as a boy who plays only to win and cannot bear defeat; watching Surya lose cheerfully and still enjoy basketball teaches him that games are for joy, and he becomes a true sportsman.
concepts.formula: old way = play only to win; new way = play to enjoy
concepts.key_idea: A defeat taken lightly by a friend turns Prabhat's fear of losing into the joy of playing.

concepts.title: Surya and the Sporting Spirit
concepts.section: Change of Heart, Let us read II
concepts.definition: Surya plays brilliantly at badminton and hopelessly at basketball with the same happy smile; his sporting spirit lies in enjoying the game for its own sake, not in the scoreboard.
concepts.key_idea: Enjoyment that does not depend on winning is the mark of sporting spirit, as Surya shows every day.

concepts.title: Winning versus Enjoying the Game
concepts.section: Change of Heart, Let us think and reflect
concepts.definition: The story argues that a scoreboard is not needed to enjoy a game; trying to do well and enjoying every moment matter more than the result of the match.
concepts.formula: enjoyment = effort + fun, not victory alone
concepts.key_idea: Prabhat wins by cheating yet feels empty, which proves that victory without joy is hollow.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Phenomenon, Significant and Defeat
concepts.section: Change of Heart, Let us learn
concepts.definition: From context, a phenomenon is someone with special qualities, significant means important, defeat means loss, and kept a close watch on means observed carefully.
concepts.key_idea: Words like phenomenon and significant raise the meaning of a sports story beyond the score.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What did Prabhat observe about Surya in the following days?

solution_template.explain: Surya cannot score for ten minutes yet keeps smiling and playing.
Prabhat sees that enjoyment never depends on the score, and this changes him.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why did Prabhat play only those games he was sure to win?

solution_template.explain: Winning felt so good that losing felt terrible to him.
To protect that feeling he avoided any game he sensed he could lose.
